content: Chloroquine phosphate is classified as an antimalarial and amebicide medication. It is prescribed to prevent and treat malaria, as well as to treat amebiasis. In some cases, it may be used for other conditions; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Chloroquine phosphate is available in tablet form and is taken orally. For malaria prevention in adults, one dose is typically taken once a week on the same day each week. Your doctor will specify the number of tablets per dose. The first dose should be taken two weeks before traveling to a malaria-endemic area, continued weekly while in the area, and for eight weeks after leaving the area. If starting two weeks prior to travel is not possible, your doctor may recommend taking a double dose immediately. For treating acute malaria attacks in adults, one dose is taken immediately, followed by half the dose 6 to 8 hours later, and then half the dose once daily for the next two days. For infants and children, the dosage is determined based on body weight, and your doctor will calculate the appropriate amount. For amebiasis treatment, one dose is taken daily for two days, followed by half the dose daily for 2 to 3 weeks. This treatment is usually combined with other amebicides. To minimize stomach upset, chloroquine phosphate should be taken with food. Follow the prescription label instructions carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed, and do not take more or less than prescribed. Chloroquine phosphate is occasionally used to alleviate symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis and to treat systemic lupus erythematosus, discoid lupus erythematosus, scleroderma, pemphigus, lichen planus, polymyositis, sarcoidosis, and porphyria cutanea tarda. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. Before using chloroquine phosphate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to chloroquine phosphate, chloroquine hydrochloride (Aralen HCl), hydroxychloroquine (Plaquenil), or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially acetaminophen (Tylenol), cimetidine (Tagamet), iron products, isoniazid (Nydrazid), kaolin, magnesium trisilicate (Gaviscon), methotrexate (Rheumatrex), niacin, rifampin (Rifadin, Rimactane), vitamins, and herbal products. Notify your doctor if you have or have had liver disease, G6PD deficiency, hearing problems, porphyria or other blood disorders, psoriasis, vision changes, weakness in your knees or ankles, or if you consume large amounts of alcohol. If you have experienced vision changes while taking chloroquine phosphate, chloroquine hydrochloride, or hydroxychloroquine, inform your doctor. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as chloroquine phosphate can harm a nursing infant. Unless otherwise instructed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking chloroquine phosphate. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Minor side effects of chloroquine phosphate may include headache, loss of appetite, diarrhea, upset stomach, stomach pain, skin rash or itching, hair loss, and mood or mental changes. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects require immediate medical attention. These include seeing light flashes or streaks, blurred vision, difficulty reading or seeing (e.g., words disappearing, misty or foggy vision), hearing difficulties, ringing in the ears, muscle weakness, drowsiness, vomiting, irregular heartbeats, convulsions, or difficulty breathing. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store chloroquine phosphate in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from light, heat, and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Children are particularly sensitive to overdose, so ensure the medication is stored securely. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order lab tests to monitor your response to chloroquine phosphate and check for muscle weakness caused by the drug. If you are taking chloroquine phosphate for an extended period, your doctor will recommend regular eye exams, as the medication can cause serious vision problems. If you notice any vision changes, stop taking chloroquine phosphate and contact your doctor immediately. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
